# Cooper — The Smallest AI Brain. Guided by a Human.

> Cooper is a local-first, human-guided AI inference engine designed for consumer hardware. It runs on a Raspberry Pi, smartphone, or old laptop — no cloud, no GPU, no subscription. Part of the ami* / BRIDGRAI ecosystem.

## About Cooper

Cooper is the smallest viable AI brain: it answers a family's real questions honestly, in six languages, on consumer hardware, with structural safety built in.

- Model-agnostic: runs any open model ≤3B parameters
- CPU-only inference, ≤2 GB RAM
- 100% local, zero telemetry
- Human-initiated only (autonomy level 0)
- DSEI 7 safety principles enforced at build time (146 automated tests)
- TVE 6-axis manipulation detection
- Anti-addiction hard-stop for minors
- Languages: Romanian, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian
- Status: In development — private beta coming 2026

## Key Differentiator

Cooper is not the model — it is the safety and governance layer around the model. Unlike running a raw model through Ollama or similar tools, Cooper enforces honest refusal structurally (not via system prompt), requires a registered human anchor for every inference, includes manipulation detection (TVE 6-axis), and runs on 2 GB RAM (vs 8–32 GB for typical local model setups).
